findings.title: Scope/implementation count mismatch: the scope says grandfathering covers "14-plus plans"; the implemented rule and --classify-requirements find exactly 12.
findings.evidence: docs/09-backlog/backlog.yaml (phase-dgov-01 scope, 3rd bullet); src/governance/requirement_rule.py:157-172, confirmed by running the CLI.
findings.consequence: Acceptance only requires "a number," which it has, so this doesn't fail R02, but the scope's own estimate doesn't match what the delivered rule measures — worth the owner noting in case "14-plus" was anchored to a different metric than "backlog items whose plan field names this doc."

findings.title: Rule is trivially gameable by splitting work across plan documents instead of phases: the mandatory condition triggers only when one plan id is named by more than one backlog item.
findings.consequence: A plan written as two single-phase plan documents instead of one two-phase plan never crosses the threshold and is never required to pair with a requirement, even though it produces the exact multi-phase, multi-session acceptance-spanning situation R01-R03 exist to catch. The written rule and the code share this gap, so a second reader applying GOV-001's prose would reach the same (wrong) permissive answer for a deliberately split plan. Not fatal to this phase's literal acceptance text, but it is a real loophole in both the rule and its enforcement.
